note: Per-construction rubrics (PLAN lever 3): committed, reviewed data. Each family lists the constructions it covers, the four scored dimensions, and a short checklist of quotable criteria the judge applies. The verdict schema stays the three-field-plus-rephrase 0|1|2 rubric (chatbench/rubric.schema.json) — no prose verdicts. familyOf() in chatbench/rubrics.mjs maps a construction (single or combo) onto one of these families.

criteria: The named term is defined from the graph's own schema vocabulary, not invented.
A term with no schema entry gets an honest miss, never a guessed gloss.
An ambiguous term (meta sense vs predicate sense) is flagged, not silently resolved one way.
The subject, verb and object all resolve to entities/edges the graph holds.
A query over an entity the graph lacks is an honest miss.
The answer cites the grounding entity id or source site where one exists.
The count matches the number of matching entities in the graph exactly.
A scoped or superlative count applies the scope before counting.
Zero matches is answered as zero, not as a miss.
The negated set is the complement of the positive set within the right universe.
"untested"/"not imported" is computed from the edges, not guessed.
An empty complement is answered as empty, honestly.
The passive's argument roles are not swapped (imported-by is the reverse of imports).
The answer names the entity on the correct side of the edge.
A role with no filler is an honest miss.
The pronoun binds to the correct prior referent, resolved from the discourse, not surface proximity.
A binding that only world knowledge could settle (Winograd-style) is either resolved correctly or honestly declined.
The final answer follows from the resolved binding.
Commit/history facts come from the graph's provenance, not invented dates or authors.
Last-touch / ordering reads respect the recorded order.
A history question the graph cannot answer is an honest miss.
A reference to a prior answer set ("which of those", "the second one") resolves against the actual prior result.
Cross-turn composition uses the earlier answers, not a re-derivation that ignores them.
When the prior context is missing or unresolvable, the answer says so rather than guessing.
Each clause is grounded and the composed answer respects the boolean/relative structure.
An elided fragment is re-instantiated into the correct prior slot.
A branch with no grounding drops out honestly rather than being filled in.
A taught fact is stored and later recalled with its provenance (the session/fact frame).
Recall cites what was told, not a fabricated source.
A recall for something never taught is an honest miss.
A true presupposition is confirmed; a false one is corrected, never silently accommodated.
An indirect speech act is answered on its intended meaning where the graph grounds it.
An unverifiable nested claim is declined, not accommodated.
The anchored, first-match template resolves the surface ambiguity without local misparsing.
The answer reflects the intended parse, grounded in the graph.
A genuinely unresolvable parse is an honest miss.
Politeness/filler noise is stripped and the underlying query answered as if clean.
The noise never changes the grounded answer.
A query that is only noise is an honest miss.
